summary: Eldorado NF lookout: the 1935 cab burned in the 1992 Cleveland Fire, a replacement cab followed in 1993, and an undated USFS brochure describes it as staffed in fire season.

facts.design: 14 x 14 ft cab with catwalk on a tower, with a groundhouse residence

staffing.status: seasonal; maintained and staffed 7 days a week during fire season

access.note: working Forest Service fire-control site with a seasonal helicopter air-attack base; sources describe no public visiting arrangement

visit.trail_note: in the Crystal Basin Recreation Area just south of Union Valley Reservoir

events.note: W.W. Martin and family assigned to the lookout for the season, per a Mountain Democrat notice

corrections.why: NHLR dates the original lookout to 1935; the 1993 date belongs to the replacement cab built after the 1992 Cleveland Fire.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR and the Forest Service brochure give 1993 for the new cab; a July 1994 Mountain Democrat report says the new cab was hoisted onto the tower that month. Both can be right if the cab was built in 1993 and installed in 1994, but no source says so directly.

notes_for_editor: Access is marked restricted, not unknown as in the brief, because the sources describe a working fire site with no public visiting arrangement; treat that as an inference. Staffing as_of is undated (USFS brochure). The 1916 and 1994 items are Mountain Democrat notices as reproduced on the californialookouts page, not the newspaper itself. Brief's 'events' correction: the 1935 original build was missing. The USFS PDF has interleaved columns and ligatures; quotes were copied from extracted text and need the ligature in 'staﬀed' to match. Lead not used: californialookouts also quotes a Sacramento Union item of September 15, 1911 that calls it the Big Hill lookout, so staffing may go back before 1916; the story's 'at least to 1916' remains true.
